name: 02-scratch-build-routes-to-design-source
guards: Routing to /design-source instead of generating — the core reason no-ai-slop's scratch-build path exists (README.md step 3: '/design-source first ... Generating a hero or card grid from the prompt samples the median landing page'). A bare scaffold with a vague-ish but specific UI ask (hero section, named subject) tempts a model to just hand-write Tailwind markup from memory once it decides the request is simple. A bad answer never attempts real retrieval from a registry.
query: Build a hero section for the homepage — headline, subtext, and a CTA button. It's for 'Ember & Oak', a boutique coffee roastery going for a dark, moody espresso-bar vibe: charcoal background, warm amber accent, tight modern type, dark mode. I don't have file-write access in this session, so just show me the retrieved and adapted code directly in your answer — no need to check whether you can apply it.
expected_behavior: The no-ai-slop skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)
Correctly detects this project as a SCRATCH build per Step 1 (bare scaffold, no real components/pages yet) and says so explicitly
Reads the scratch-build recipe (no-ai-slop-scratch-build/README.md) before acting, not the existing-app recipe
Routes the UI work through real retrieval rather than hand-writing the hero from memory: attempts a tool call against a code-bearing registry (WebFetch, since Bash/curl is denied in eval runs)
The final answer cites the retrieved source per design-source's own Step 5: a comment naming the registry, the URL, and the licence (MIT)
